docs.title: MSF Laravel Common
docs.text: msflib/common is the shared foundation package for the wider MSF Laravel ecosystem. It provides reusable common models, GraphQL schema fragments, provider registration, and migration support so downstream packages can build on a consistent base rather than duplicating the same patterns across the stack.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
This package is designed to provide the common structural layer for Laravel applications built with MSF components.

It is responsible for:

  • service-provider registration in Laravel
  • shared GraphQL types and reusable schema fragments
  • model conventions for common domain entities
  • database migration support for shared catalog data

docs.title: Key integration points
docs.text:
The package registers its GraphQL schema by listening to Lighthouse schema build events and stitching the package-level schema into the app schema.

Event::listen(BuildSchemaString::class, function ($schemaString) use ($graphql) {
    return (new SchemaStitcher($graphql))->getSchemaString();
});

This pattern keeps the common schema modular while allowing the application to assemble a single composite GraphQL schema at runtime.

docs.title: Composer installation
docs.text:
composer require msflib/common

The package declares msflib/graphql as a dependency, so it assumes the downstream app is already configured for Lighthouse-based GraphQL work.

docs.title: Package types and model conventions
docs.text:
The included GraphQL schema defines reusable content types such as:

  • Category
  • Status

These are common reference entities that can be extended or consumed by higher-level business packages.

docs.title: Development workflow
docs.text:
Local package validation is handled through the package-level Laravel Testbench setup:

composer install
composer test

The package also exposes lint and formatting tools such as:

composer lint

docs.title: Common package
docs.text: The msflib/common package is the reusable foundation for shared Laravel models, schema fragments, and common domain metadata. It keeps shared logic in one place so package consumers do not need to duplicate repeated CRUD and catalog patterns.

docs.title: Package responsibilities
docs.text:
This package focuses on:

  • service-provider registration in Laravel apps
  • shared migration support
  • reusable GraphQL schema slices
  • common reference-domain models such as categories and statuses

docs.title: Service provider
docs.text:
The package registers its boot logic in MsfCommonServiceProvider:

class MsfCommonServiceProvider extends ServiceProvider
{
    public function boot()
    {
        $graphql = __DIR__ . '/../graphql/schema.graphql';
        if (file_exists($graphql)) {
            Event::listen(BuildSchemaString::class, function ($schemaString) use ($graphql) {
                return (new SchemaStitcher($graphql))->getSchemaString();
            });
        }

        $this->loadMigrationsFrom(__DIR__ . '/../database/migrations');
    }
}

This ensures the package’s schema and migrations are automatically included when the Laravel app boots.

docs.title: Shared data model patterns
docs.text:
The package is meant to hold common catalog-style entities and metadata types that many app modules can use. Examples in the schema include:

  • category metadata
  • status metadata
  • relationships between shared resources

These patterns are intentionally generic and reusable, rather than being tied to a single product or business domain.

docs.title: Laravel integration
docs.text:
The package registers the provider like this in Composer metadata:

"extra": {
  "laravel": {
    "providers": [
      "Msflib\\Common\\MsfCommonServiceProvider",
      "Msflib\\GraphQl\\MsfGraphQlServiceProvider"
    ]
  }
}

This keeps app bootstrapping consistent with the rest of the MSF package ecosystem.

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
use Msflib\Common\Models\Category;

$category = Category::query()->first();

The package is intended to offer shared catalog and metadata primitives rather than domain-specific business logic.

docs.title: GraphQL schema
docs.text: The msflib/common package contributes a reusable GraphQL schema fragment for shared entities and metadata types. It is stitched into the app schema at runtime through Lighthouse’s schema build pipeline.

docs.title: Schema entry point
docs.text:
The package defines its GraphQL operations under graphql/schema.graphql and exposes types such as:

  • Category
  • Status

The schema includes query and mutation support for listing, finding, creating, updating, and deleting these resources.

docs.title: Example schema fragment
docs.text:
type Category @model(class: "\\Msflib\\Common\\Models\\Category") {
    id: ID!
    name: String!
    description: String!
    category: Category
    products: [Product!]!
    created_at: DateTimeTz
    updated_at: DateTimeTz
}

The package intentionally keeps these resource definitions generic, so they can be reused or extended by downstream application packages.

docs.title: Stitching model
docs.text: The service provider listens for Lighthouse’s BuildSchemaString event and merges the package schema into the application’s schema. This is how the common package contributes to the overall GraphQL API without requiring the application to manually import its schema files.

docs.title: Usage notes
docs.text:
• define shared primitives in this package rather than app-specific mutations
  • keep schema names consistent with the domain model names
  • use validation rules in the schema input types for field-level constraints
